catalogTitle: בגלות ראשון בא אליהו - גואל אחרון

oneLiner.en: From the count of seventy souls who went down to Egypt, the Mashgiach shows that the start of every Jewish galus already carries the geulah, and that Eliyahu Hanavi, the herald of the redemption, enters the galus together with the Jews.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach asks why the seventy souls who came to Egypt number only sixty-nine, and what 'pearl' lies in the answer that Yocheved was born between the walls as they entered. He explains that a Jewish galus must contain geulah: the Midrash says Moshiach was born on the day of the churban, and Pesach and Tisha b'Av fall on the same weekday. Yocheved, mother of the redeemer, was born at the very first step into galus, and Hashem Himself joins the count and goes into exile with His people. The Midrash also says Serach completed the count and is reckoned as two: since she brought Yaakov the news that Yosef lives, a spark of Eliyahu joined her, so she entered Gan Eden alive. Thus the seventieth soul was Eliyahu, herald of the geulah. The Mashgiach then describes Klal Yisroel's growth in exile and turns to the shtiebel: a warm place of unity where all who seek Hashem feel at home.

en: A Jewish galus is not like the exile of other nations: it must contain the geulah from its very beginning.
Yocheved, from whom Moshe came, was born exactly as the Jews passed between the walls into Egypt, showing that the first step of galus is also the first step of geulah.
Hashem Himself completes the count of seventy and goes down with the Jews into exile, as Yechezkel saw the whole Merkavah in Bavel.
Serach is counted as two because a spark of Eliyahu Hanavi joined her when she told Yaakov that Yosef lives, so the seventieth soul to enter Egypt was in truth Eliyahu, herald of the geulah.

Each stage in the growth of Klal Yisroel, from Avraham to the shevatim to the seventy souls to the nation of six hundred thousand, happened outside Eretz Yisroel and under hardship, and this is the purpose of galus.
The shtiebel is meant to be a small corner of light in galus, a place of unity where Jews of every group can come together, feel at home and serve Hashem.

title.en: Seventy souls, but only sixty-nine

summary.en: After a few opening words, the Mashgiach brings that exactly seventy souls had to come down to Egypt, and asks how, since only sixty-nine are listed. He cites the answer that Yocheved was born between the walls, which an Amora called a precious pearl, and asks what pearl lies in it.

title.en: The Midrash: Hashem and Serach complete the count

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings two more answers of the Midrash: that Hashem Himself completes the seventy, and that Serach bas Asher completes the count. He cites the Yefeh To'ar that Serach, who lived on and entered Gan Eden alive, is counted as two, and asks why her long life should make her count as two.

title.en: Galus that already holds the geulah

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Midrash that on the day the Beis Hamikdash was destroyed Moshiach was born, and that Pesach and Tisha b'Av fall on the same weekday. He explains that a Jewish churban is unlike that of the nations, so galus must contain geulah, and adds the Midrash on 'Mizmor l'Asaf' and the Shechinah going into exile with the Jews as a guarantee of redemption.

title.en: Yocheved born at the first step of galus

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Midrash of the woman who bore six hundred thousand, which Rabbeinu Bachya reads as the Shechinah, and gives two explanations of the pearl: Yocheved, mother of Moshe, was born at the very step that began the galus, a sign the geulah is certain; and Hashem joins the count and goes into exile with the Jews, as Yechezkel saw the Merkavah in Bavel.

title.en: Serach and the spark of Eliyahu

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains why Serach is counted as two: the sefarim say that one who brings good tidings is joined by a spark of Eliyahu, and he tells the story of the Yesod HaAvodah who climbed up at night to bring his grandson good news. Since Yaakov was all of Klal Yisroel, Serach's news that Yosef lives was like Eliyahu announcing Moshiach; Eliyahu joined her, so she could not die and is counted as two.

title.en: Eliyahu enters galus first

summary.en: The Mashgiach concludes that the last of the seventy to enter Egypt was Eliyahu Hanavi, herald of the geulah: galus cannot begin without him. He suggests this is why Eliyahu is mentioned on Motzaei Shabbos, the passage from Shabbos, likened to Eretz Yisroel, into the weekdays, and connects the three days of darkness from the eighth of Teves and the song about Eliyahu just sung.

title.en: Klal Yisroel grows in exile

summary.en: The Mashgiach traces the stages of Klal Yisroel: Avraham born outside the Land, the shevatim born in chutz la'aretz, the seventy completed between the walls, the nation formed in Egypt. Every stage came in galus and hardship, so the deeper the galus the greater the growth; souls came into the world for the work of galus, and what was achieved in it will one day be revealed.

title.en: The shtiebel: hold together in the dark

summary.en: The Mashgiach says one must thank Hashem for every bit of light in the deep darkness before Moshiach, and calls the shtiebel an embassy of holiness. He brings R' Shmuel of Kaminka on 'gather together', the Rizhiner's counsel to meet on Shabbos and strengthen one another, the Ba'al Shem Tov's three loves, and Rebbe Elimelech's prayer for ahavas chaverim.

title.en: A home for every kind of Jew

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the shtiebel as a place without factions, where chassidim of every court and every kind of Jew feel at home because all serve one Ribono shel Olam. He warns that the Satan works against every good thing, says Hashem does not want one group alone serving Him, and links unity to the haftorah of the two sticks of Yosef and Yehudah.

title.en: Crumbs under the table; a davenshtub

summary.en: The Mashgiach applies 'Vayigash' to the coming together of Yehudah and Yosef and says the little chassidus left today must unite and gather its crumbs, as the Midrash speaks of hunger before Moshiach. He wants the shtiebel to warm anyone with a heavy heart, and brings the Divrei Chaim's teshuvah that a tzaddik's place of prayer is a 'davenshtub', not a beis haknesses, made also for eating and rejoicing together.

title.en: Why a 'shtiebel': the small upper room

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains the name 'shtiebel' through the small upper room the Shunamite made for Elisha, kept small so Gechazi would not come in: the place should be wide for those who seek Hashem and too narrow for those who come for honor or gain. He closes with a tefillah that Hashem establish the work of their hands, that Eliyahu and Moshiach be revealed, and that they merit to go up to Eretz Yisroel.

catalogTitle: מ'געזעגנט זיך פון ספר בראשית! ספר של ספורי צדיקים

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains that the closed parsha of Vayechi teaches that the true life of Yaakov, and the real purpose of a Jew, is found in the darkness of galus, where one must serve Hashem with strength and say chazak.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the Midrash's reasons why Vayechi is a closed parsha, and connects the filled space to Rebbi Yehudah HaNasi, a gilgul of Yaakov, who wrote down the Oral Torah that belongs in the white space of the Torah. From the Gemara that Yaakov did not die he shows that Yaakov's strength lives on in his children even far in exile. He ties this to the long dark nights of Teves and to the present darkness of galus, and explains that Yaakov truly lived in Mitzrayim because the purpose of the soul's descent is to reveal Hashem's kingship in darkness, not in the light of Shabbos. Bereishis ends with Yosef's coffin sunk by sorcery, which is the time to cry chazak. He closes with the weeks of Shovavim, the learning of Yevamos as a tikkun of the soul, and a Slonimer chassid's seven jokes.

en: The Mashgiach explains that the white space around the letters of a Sefer Torah holds the Oral Torah, and Rebbi, a gilgul of Yaakov, wrote it down only because of the troubles of exile; this is hinted in the filled space before Vayechi.
According to the Mashgiach, the strength of Yaakov was passed on to his children and never died, so even when they are far off and in captivity Yaakov lives with them.

The Mashgiach explains that the purpose of the soul's descent from beneath the Throne of Glory is to reveal Hashem's kingship specifically in a place of darkness, so the weekdays and galus are the main arena of avodah, not Shabbos.
He teaches that a Jew is measured not by his Shabbos table but by whether he stays standing in the night, as the passuk calls the servants of Hashem those who stand in His house at night.
The Mashgiach explains that Yaakov did reveal the end of days: the end will come precisely when the eyes and hearts of Yisrael are closed and it seems impossible that Moshiach could come.
When Bereishis closes with Yosef's coffin sunk by sorcery and the forces of the other side seem to win, the Mashgiach says one must not despair but cry chazak and declare Hashem's kingship.

The Mashgiach explains that Yevamos, the masechta being learned now in the weeks of Shovavim, deals with tikkun hanefesh, and therefore it comes with difficulty, because repairing the soul is not easy.

title.en: Why Vayechi is a closed parsha

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why there is no break between Vayigash and Vayechi and brings the Midrash's three reasons: the hearts of Yisrael were closed by the bondage, Yaakov wanted to reveal the end, and all troubles were hidden from him. He adds that Rebbi lived seventeen years in Tzippori, applied the passuk of Vayechi to himself, and was a gilgul of Yaakov.

title.en: The white space, Rebbi, and Yaakov who lives

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the white margin of a Sefer Torah is the Oral Torah, brings a letter that left a blank space for the reader to understand, and shows that Rebbi hinted himself in the filled space because he wrote down the Oral Torah due to the troubles of exile. He then explains the Gemara that Yaakov did not die: Yaakov's strength lives on in his children even when they are far away.

title.en: The long nights of Teves and of galus

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the season of the longest nights as a time of middas hadin, explains warmth and cold as chesed and din, and calls the present the longest night in the history of the Jewish people. He brings the Gemara about Adam HaRishon and the lengthening nights, and the custom not to learn on the longest night.

title.en: Yaakov truly lived in Mitzrayim

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why the Torah says Yaakov 'lived' in Mitzrayim, the most impure land, and explains that Yaakov is the root of the Jews in galus. One must not despair in exile; Hashem sent each Jew there with a mission, and even in a closed place without room for a break, Yaakov lives.

title.en: The purpose of creation: avodah in the dark

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the soul came down from the Throne of Glory to reveal Hashem's kingship in darkness, and that light and joy in avodah are already a reward. He brings Reb Zusha and the Lechovitcher's parable of a traveler at an inn to show that Shabbos is a rest along the way, while the weekdays are the real purpose.

title.en: Chazak at the end of Bereishis

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that Bereishis ends sadly with the deaths of Yaakov and Yosef, and says this is the time to cry chazak. He teaches that a Jew is measured in the night, not at his Shabbos table, and brings the Kozhnitzer Maggid that from Vayeshev until Vayechi Hashem's name of mercy does not appear because galus was beginning.

title.en: Hoping to Hashem in every state

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that in every situation, light or dark, one must turn to Hashem, using the words 'lishuascha kivisi Hashem' and Yaakov's disappointment when he thought Shimshon was Moshiach. He adds that one must remember Hashem even in calm times, and brings Yehudah's greatness: even crouching, he remains a lion.

title.en: Closed hearts and the hidden end

summary.en: From Rashi's words the Mashgiach shows that a Jew's heart affects the Torah itself, brings Reb Tzadok's Pri Tzaddik on Vayechi, and then asks why the Torah records Yaakov's attempt to reveal the end if he failed. He answers that the closing itself is the revelation: Moshiach will come precisely when hearts are closed.

title.en: Bereishis ends with sorcery

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Bereishis is the book of creation, in which Hashem's light descended until one could even deny Him, and that it ends with the Egyptians sinking Yosef's coffin in the Nile by sorcery, which denies the heavenly household. At such a time one must not despair but cry chazak and say Aleinu.

title.en: Souls bound to chutz la'aretz and darkness

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the letter of Reb Mendel of Vitebsk that some souls belong to Eretz Yisrael and some to chutz la'aretz, and that the Baal HaTanya was shown from heaven to stay. He explains that certain repairs of the soul can only be made in darkness and weekday struggle, and that when hopes are dashed as at Yosef's death one must cry chazak.

title.en: Shovavim and learning Yevamos

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that after Vayechi come the weeks of Shovavim, a time of tikkun hanefesh for Klal Yisrael and for each Jew. He explains that each masechta carries its own light, sees hashgachah in the yeshivos learning Yevamos now, and explains that Yevamos deals with tikkun hanefesh and therefore comes with toil.

title.en: One step at a time: the seven jokes

summary.en: The Mashgiach returns to the traveler in the storm: a Jew in a period of trials must toil and know he will arrive at the day that is all Shabbos. He says one should take it calmly, one day and one task at a time, and closes with a Slonimer chassid who walked a long journey with 'seven jokes'.

catalogTitle: ויחי יעקב - דוקא בגלות' כי שם עיקר עבודת יהודי

oneLiner.en: Taking leave of Sefer Bereishis with Vayechi, the Mashgiach shows that Yaakov and Yosef reached their greatest kedushah davka in Egypt, and that in the darkness of exile a Jew acquires kedushah and Eretz Yisrael through Torah and tefillah.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the sadness of parting from Sefer Bereishis, which holds the hidden point of what a Jew is, and urges learning the stories of the Avos and Shevatim in depth. Bereishis ends with Yaakov, who stands for kedushah, as the praise of Shemoneh Esrei ends with HaKel HaKadosh. Rabbeinu HaKadosh, who said Vayechi was written about him, carried Yaakov's kedushah; the Mashgiach explains why Vayechi is a closed parsha: Rebbe wrote the Oral Torah down because of the exile. Yosef, the inner kedushah of Yaakov, grew great davka in Egypt and on the idolaters' festival day, and so a young man today who turns away from the screen can become a Yosef. The Mashgiach explains why Yosef made his brothers swear to carry his bones, and closes with Shechem and Kiryas Sefer: Eretz Yisrael is acquired with Torah and tefillah, the true teshuvah of Shovavim.

en: Sefer Bereishis, the stories of the Avos and Shevatim, holds the hidden point of the Jewish soul, and learned in depth it leaves a lasting impression of yiras Shamayim.
Yaakov is the attribute of kedushah, and only one who draws kedushah upon himself can truly praise Hashem; therefore the praises of Shemoneh Esrei end with HaKel HaKadosh.
Rabbeinu HaKadosh, who identified himself with Yaakov, wrote down the Oral Torah because of the exile, and this is hinted in the Torah by Vayechi being a closed parsha.
Yosef did not become great in his father's holy home but davka in impure Egypt, and so in a generation full of temptation each young man who holds back can become a Yosef.

Yosef had his brothers swear to carry up his bones because his bones came from Yaakov, so their burial in Eretz Yisrael completed his father's burial, and the brothers were more obligated in Yaakov's honor than his grandchildren.
Eretz Yisrael, like Shechem which Yaakov took 'with his sword and bow', meaning his wisdom and prayer, is acquired with Torah and tefillah, which is also the main teshuvah of Shovavim.

Rabbeinu HaKadosh and the writing of the Mishnah
Eretz Yisrael through Torah and tefillah

title.en: Parting from Sefer Bereishis

summary.en: The Mashgiach says it is hard to part from Bereishis and brings Reb Baruch'l of Mezhibuzh's saying on why the Torah began with it. Bereishis is the hidden point of the Jew, as shown by a story of the Baal Shem Tov with a poritz, and the stories of the Avos and tzaddikim awaken yiras Shamayim.

title.en: The greatness of the Avos and Shevatim

summary.en: The Mashgiach tells how a sefer of stories of tzaddikim shaped him as a boy, and shows the Avos' self-sacrifice: Avraham for whom this world was the small heh, Yehudah the king offering himself as a slave for Binyamin, Yaakov serving the same way for twenty-two years without ruach hakodesh, and Yosef withstanding the tortures of Potiphar's wife.

title.en: HaKel HaKadosh: praise needs kedushah

summary.en: Bereishis ends with Yaakov just as the first three brachos of Shemoneh Esrei, set against the Avos, end with HaKel HaKadosh. The Mashgiach explains that only one who strives for kedushah can sing Hashem's praise, as the ofanim rise to the seraphim by saying kadosh, and that this is Yaakov's lesson alongside Avraham's love and Yitzchak's fear.

title.en: Rabbeinu HaKadosh and Yosef: Yaakov's kedushah

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Midrash that Rebbe applied 'Vayechi Yaakov' to his own seventeen years in Tzippori, showing that he carried Yaakov's soul and kedushah, which is why he alone is called HaKadosh. Yaakov's inner kedushah was revealed in Yosef, the attribute of yesod, whose time is the weeks of Shovavim that begin after Vayechi.

title.en: Vayechi in Egypt and the closed parsha

summary.en: Yaakov taught Yosef the six orders of Mishnah hinted in 'zekunim', and Rebbe, Yaakov's gilgul, redacted and wrote the Mishnah because the exile made it forgotten. The Mashgiach brings Rashi that Vayechi is closed and explains the spaces between parshiyos: the white around the black letters of the Sefer Torah is the Oral Torah.

title.en: Rebbe hinted in the Torah; Shema at night

summary.en: Where the white space between Vayigash and Vayechi should be, it is written over, just as Rebbe wrote the Oral Torah because of the exile; that is where Rebbe is hinted. The Mishnah opens with Shema at night, the words the Shevatim said to Yaakov, continuing Yaakov's acceptance of Heaven's yoke in the darkness of exile, which the Mashgiach says one must carry through the year.

title.en: Yosef's eyes and the mezuzah's kedushah

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Alshich on 'Ben poras Yosef, ben poras alei ayin': Yosef's greatness came through guarding his eyes. He urges taking enough kedushah from Vayechi for Shovavim and the year, and explains from the Shulchan Aruch that a mezuzah brings kedushah into the home and that where there is no kedushah impurity enters.

title.en: Davka in Egypt: growth amid impurity

summary.en: The Mashgiach speaks of the television, which even the nations admit brings bad traits, and answers the claim that one cannot help it: Egypt was the most impure land, yet Yosef grew great davka there and not in his father's home. Holding back amid impurity raises a person more than a holy Seder night, and he touches on Nittel, the long dark night of the idolaters' festival.

title.en: Every bachur can be a Yosef

summary.en: On 'Vayehi kehayom hazeh' Rashi says it was the Egyptians' festival day, which a sefer identifies as Nittel; on that most impure day Yosef became the holiest. The Mashgiach describes how precious in Heaven is a young man who turns from the screen to a blatt Gemara, and closes Bereishis with chazak and the teaching that Yaakov avinu did not die.

title.en: Yosef's answer and the oath to his brothers

summary.en: Yaakov on his deathbed asks Yosef to bury him in Me'aras HaMachpelah, and per a Midrash Yosef answers that he too will ask to be taken out. The Mashgiach sharpens the question: why speak of himself at such a moment, and why make his brothers and not his own children swear? Midos chassidus one does not command another, as 'an am ha'aretz is not a chassid'.

title.en: Tzaddikim do not decay; bones from the father

summary.en: Yosef did not decay in Egypt, and the Mashgiach tells of a Jew he knew who was among ten forced by the Germans to dig at Reb Elimelech's grave in Lizhensk and found him whole; Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon also stayed whole. He brings the Gemara that a person's bones come from his father, and that some life remains in a tzaddik's grave, which is why one davens there.

title.en: Completing Yaakov's burial

summary.en: The Mashgiach answers: since Yosef's bones come from Yaakov, Yosef promised more than asked, that even his own bones would be brought up as the completion of his father's burial. Because one is more obligated in a father's honor than a grandfather's, he told the brothers, and wanted all twelve tribes' bones brought up, as Rashi on 'itchem' says.

title.en: Yaakov lives on; Torah the key to Kiryas Sefer

summary.en: Yaakov did not die: as long as his children live like him his kedushah remains, and Yaakov is Torah, the key to everything. Yaakov's words to Yosef about Shechem lead the Mashgiach to Kiryas Sefer, which the Gemara says means the three thousand forgotten halachos; a sefer he links to the Baal Shem Tov explains that the land was written with them, so Osniel, who restored them, could conquer it.

title.en: Shechem, Yosef's place of kedushas habris

summary.en: Shechem is Yosef's place, the place of kedushas habris, which is why the outrage there was so grave and Shimon and Levi took revenge. Yaakov took it 'with his sword and bow', which Rashi renders his wisdom and prayer: he learned and innovated Torah and so could conquer it. The Mashgiach reads this as advice for acquiring Eretz Yisrael and turns to the current debate over the territories.

title.en: What is discussed below is judged above

summary.en: The Mashgiach declines to decide the question of the territories, leaving it to the gedolim, but says that what the whole world speaks about is a sign of what is being judged in Heaven, as with Haman's slander. For believing Jews the only counsel is Torah and tefillah, since with every halachah learned one acquires a piece of Eretz Yisrael.

title.en: Shechem today, Shovavim and Torah

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that the Arabs call Shechem Nablus, recalling the 'nevalah' done there, and that the worst murderers gather there; Shechem is acquired only with Torah and tefillah. He ties this to Shovavim, whose main teshuvah is Torah, and closes with the wish to feel the sweetness of Bereishis and merit the full redemption.

catalogTitle: The Seeds of Redemption are Sown as כלל ישראל Enters גלות

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach shows from Vayigash that Klal Yisrael's darkest moments carry the seeds of redemption: 'Ani Yosef' came at the bleakest point, and the seventieth soul that went down to Mitzrayim, Serach with Eliyahu in her or Yocheved the mother of the redeemer, shows that no galus comes without geulah.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the Ishbitzer's reading of Vayigash as 'Vey, Yidden shreit gevalt' and explains that the parsha is a preface to galus. The Shevatim had lost Yosef HaTzaddik, root of Moshiach ben Yosef, and now Yehuda, seed of Moshiach ben David, offered himself as a slave; in that darkest moment came 'Ani Yosef'. He applies this to Klal Yisrael's situation today among Yishmael and, from Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer, explains the name Yishmael as a promise that Hashem will hear the cry of the last galus. Vayigash falls in the darkest time of year, before Asara b'Teves and the tekufah. He then asks who completes the seventy souls, brings the Yefei To'ar on Serach, and answers through the Meor Einayim that Serach, who told Yaakov 'Od Yosef chai', carried Eliyahu in her. Galus is rooted in geulah. He closes by explaining the tekufah, the calendar and Nittel.

en: Vayigash is the preface to galus: its first part shows the darkest moment turning into 'Ani Yosef', and then the descent to Mitzrayim begins.
With Yosef lost and Yehuda about to become a slave, the Shevatim seemed to lose both Moshiach ben Yosef and Moshiach ben David, and at that moment the redemption appeared.
According to Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer the name Yishmael means 'Hashem will hear': when Klal Yisrael cries out under Yishmael's oppression, they are promised an answer.
The seventieth soul that completes the count of those who went down to Mitzrayim, Serach carrying Eliyahu or Yocheved the mother of Moshe, shows that every galus comes together with geulah.
By the At-Bash pairing the first day of Pesach falls on the same weekday as Tisha B'Av, because galus is rooted in geulah.
Tekufas Teves, the longest night, is the time when the forces of tumah are strongest, and the Mashgiach explains how the calendar places Nittel on it.

the seventy souls who went down to Mitzrayim

title.en: 'Vey, Yidden shreit gevalt'; who is called HaTzaddik

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Pri Tzaddik quoting the Ishbitzer that the letters of Vayigash spell 'Vey, Yidden shreit gevalt', and says the parsha has a preface and a long story. Explaining that only Yosef is called HaTzaddik, he digresses on the few great ones called HaKadosh and on the ruach hakodesh of all Klal Yisrael that the Kuzari describes, which is why a minhag is binding.

title.en: Losing Yosef and Yehuda, then 'Ani Yosef'

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that the Shevatim felt the loss of the hidden tzaddik Yosef, from whom Moshiach ben Yosef comes, and now Yehuda, the open leader who carries Moshiach ben David, offered himself as a slave for Binyamin. In that darkest moment came 'Ani Yosef', a sign that Hashem will reveal Himself when all hope seems lost.

title.en: Klal Yisrael's dark moment today

summary.en: The Mashgiach applies the lesson to the present: Jews surrounded by hostile Arab nations, the Rambam's words about Yishmael, the Chafetz Chaim's reply to a man going to Eretz Yisrael, and Rav Savitsky's report that by nature only Moshiach can help now.

title.en: Galus begins; the meaning of the name Yishmael

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that after the preface the descent to Mitzrayim begins, so Vayigash is the parsha of galus. He brings Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer that Yishmael is named for 'Yishma Kel v'ya'anem', asks how this fits the passuk's own reason, and answers that the passuk itself promises Hashem will hear Klal Yisrael when Yishmael oppresses them.

title.en: Vayigash in the darkest time of the year

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Vayigash is read in Teves, the Shabbos before Asara b'Teves, which the Abudraham says would be fasted even on Shabbos because the beginning of the churban is the worst, and often near the tekufah, the longest night. This year the tekufah coincides with Asara b'Teves, so he says great salvation can be expected.

title.en: Who completes the seventy souls?

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the question that only sixty-nine are counted among those who went down to Mitzrayim: the Gemara answers Yocheved, born at the gates of Mitzrayim, and the Medrash answers Hashem or Serach bas Asher. He brings the Yefei To'ar, who explains that Serach, who lived long and saved Avel Beis Maachah, was so important she counts as two, and asks why then Yosef, who saved the world, is not counted as two.

title.en: Eliyahu and good news; Serach tells Yaakov

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Meor Einayim that Eliyahu HaNavi enters, for a time, a person who tells good news, which is why people rush to be first, and makes it an opportune time for teshuvah. He then tells the Medrash that the Shevatim feared to tell Yaakov that Yosef was alive, and young Serach sang it to him until he believed, and he blessed her to live long and enter Gan Eden alive.

title.en: Serach counted as two: galus rooted in geulah

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that because Yaakov embodied all Klal Yisrael, Serach's good news was like Eliyahu's announcement of Moshiach, so Eliyahu stayed in her for life; she is Serach and Eliyahu, and so counts as two. Whether the seventieth is Eliyahu, Yocheved the mother of the redeemer, or Hashem, galus never comes without geulah, as the At-Bash pairing of Pesach with Tisha B'Av shows.

title.en: Adam HaRishon and the longest night

summary.en: Turning to the twenty-fifth of December, the Mashgiach brings the Gemara that Adam HaRishon, seeing the days shorten after his sin, fasted until tekufas Teves and made a festival when the days began to lengthen. He explains that all tekufos are dangerous, as the Shulchan Aruch's laws about water show, and the longest night most of all.

title.en: The calendar: Shmuel's tekufah and the twelve days

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains the solar and lunar years and the added Adar that keeps Pesach in the spring, and the dispute between Shmuel and Rav Ada on the tekufah, where the halacha follows Shmuel though his reckoning drifts. The non-Jews took over this reckoning and later dropped days to correct it, which is why their December twenty-fifth sits near the tekufah.

title.en: Two Nittels; Yosef's test; the darkest Shabbos

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains why there are two Nittel dates and the customs of not learning that night, and says each should follow his parents' minhag. He connects Yosef's test to that day, the 'yom eid' Rashi describes, when Torah study was not available to him, and closes that this Shabbos, at the exact tekufah and the darkest day, is a happy Shabbos when Moshiach can come.

catalogTitle: נסתמו עיניהם ולבם של ישראל מצרות השעיבוד- ובכל זאת -ויחי יעקב

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach explains why Parshas Vayechi is 'closed', why the end of the galus is hidden, and teaches that in the very closed space stand the words 'Vayechi Yaakov': the emunah of Yaakov lives on in Klal Yisrael even in the darkest night of the galus.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with Rashi's two reasons why Parshas Vayechi is 'closed': the hearts and eyes of Yisrael were closed by the bondage, and Yaakov wished to reveal the end and it was hidden from him. Since the Jews are the Torah, their state shows in the Torah. Yaakov found no ches or tes in the names of the tribes, so knowing the end was no part of their mission. The Mashgiach gives reasons why the end is hidden: it must stay open to 'achishenah', not knowing is part of the galus, and every great good is hidden from the Satan. A long digression on covering drinks, the Gemara of the pilegesh of Givah and the traits of a ger leads to the almanah, a picture of Knesses Yisrael in galus, exposed to the 'snake'. He ends that in the closed space stand the words 'Vayechi Yaakov': Yaakov lives, emunah survives, and those who waited for the redemption will be the most precious.

en: Parshas Vayechi is 'closed' because the eyes and hearts of Yisrael were closed by the bondage, and since the Jews are the Torah, their state is mirrored in it.
Yaakov saw no ches or tes in the names of the tribes; knowing the end is not the mission of a Jew, who must daven for the redemption without making calculations.
The end is hidden so that it is not fixed and can come early, because not knowing is part of the galus, and because every great good must be hidden from the Satan.
Knesses Yisrael in galus is called an almanah; like a widow who is not careful about uncovered drinks, in galus the yiras shamayim is weakened and the Jews are exposed to the 'snake'.
In the space where the parsha should be open stand the words 'Vayechi Yaakov': the emunah Yaakov planted lives on in Klal Yisrael even when nothing can be seen.
The Jews who waited for the redemption through the darkest times will be the most precious, and for them Hashem has prepared the wine kept since creation.

title.en: Why Parshas Vayechi is closed

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings a Midrash through Rabbeinu Bachya that Yaakov's seventeen years in Egypt repaid the seventeen years he raised Yosef, then Rashi's reason that the parsha is closed because the hearts and eyes of Yisrael were closed. Since the Jews are the Torah, their state shows in it; he adds the closed mem of 'lemarbeh hamisrah' and that the parsha speaks of the redemption.

title.en: No ches and tes in the names of the tribes

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Yaakov wanted to reveal the end but saw no ches or tes in the names of the tribes. A person's name hints at his mission, so he understood that knowing the end is not the mission of a Jew; one must daven to Hashem like a child to a parent, without calculating the end.

title.en: Why the end is hidden

summary.en: The Mashgiach gives reasons why the end is hidden: a revealed end would be fixed and could not come early, the Maharal says not knowing is part of the galus, and every great good is hidden so that the Satan should not accuse. He shows this in Moshiach's hidden lineage, the covered shofar, matzah and challos, and in kosher wine that a goy's touch spoils.

title.en: Covering drinks from the snake

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains why the Gemara requires covering drinks because of the snake: a Jew is refined and sensitive, and the holier a thing is, the more easily it is spoiled, while a goy is not harmed. He brings the Shelah that the snake is a spiritual force, so a ba'al nefesh is careful even today.

title.en: The fly and the hair of the pilegesh

summary.en: As a digression, the Mashgiach takes up the difficult Gemara about the pilegesh of Givah, where Rabbi Evyasar says a fly was found and Rabbi Yonasan a hair, and both are true, and asks what happened if the husband did not mind the fly. He brings Tosafos that she was a bas yefas toar, and explains that a ger keeps every mitzvah like a Jew but the inherited traits of the seed of the avos, like mercy and modesty, come from yichus.

title.en: Is a ger a child of Avraham?

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks whether a ger receives the traits of the Jewish soul. The Mishnah in Bikkurim says a ger cannot say 'our fathers', while the Yerushalmi says he can, since Avraham is 'father of a multitude of nations', and the Rambam and Shulchan Aruch follow it. He then brings the Gemara that Shmuel would not drink water from a widow's house, who is not careful about uncovered water, but did drink from a goy.

title.en: Cleanliness, and the answer about the pilegesh

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that goyim are more careful about outward cleanliness, like Esav who shows his 'kosher hooves', though cleanliness is a real path to kedushah. Returning to the Gemara, he answers that the husband did not mind the fly, but the hair showed she lacked the traits of the daughters of Yisrael, so the fly was revealed in hindsight as negligence: both opinions are true.

title.en: Why the punishment for Michah's idol waited

summary.en: The Mashgiach stresses that nothing happens by chance, and brings the Maharal that from the punishment one learns the sin, as with Kamtza and bar Kamtza. The Gemara in Chelek says the tens of thousands fell at Givah because no one protested Michah's idol; the punishment waited until the Jews showed at Givah that they could fight for a person's honor, revealing in hindsight that they could have fought for Hashem's.

title.en: Knesses Yisrael as an almanah

summary.en: The Mashgiach asks why the widow is not careful about uncovered water, since gilui is a real prohibition. He explains that Knesses Yisrael in galus is called an almanah, 'for the man is not at home': in galus the eyes and heart are closed, the yetzer hara grows strong, and the fear of Heaven that came from Yerushalayim is missing.

title.en: The longest night of the galus

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the end of the galus as the longest night, falling around Parshas Vayechi, darker than even the Chanukah lights can reach. The Jews are exposed to the snake and the end is hidden; he brings the Midrash of Yaakov's ladder, where the present galus seemed to have no end.

title.en: In the closed space: 'Vayechi Yaakov'

summary.en: The Mashgiach teaches that in the space of nine letters that is missing stand the words 'Vayechi Yaakov': Yaakov lives, and so does the emunah he planted. He ties Yaakov to Shabbos and the third Beis HaMikdash, explains why Melaveh Malkah mentions Yaakov, who 'did not die', and tells of the Kotzker and Reb Meir of Apta to show that believing is greater than seeing.

title.en: The reward of those who waited

summary.en: The Mashgiach concludes that precisely holding on to emunah in the darkest times can bring Moshiach, and that those who waited will be the most precious when they see Moshiach crowned. For them Hashem has kept the wine no eye has seen; the one thing that saves in these long nights is to hold on to emunah and bitachon.

catalogTitle: נסיונות של סוף גלות מצרים ונסיונות זמנינו

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach shows that at the end of every exile, just as the salvation begins to shine, the darkness grows worse, as with Yosef's brothers, with Moshe in Mitzrayim and in his own generation, and he urges Jews to keep hoping for Moshiach.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the end of Sefer Bereishis: after twenty-two years of Yosef's concealment, Yaakov sensed hope in Mitzrayim, yet things grew worse, Shimon and Binyamin were taken and the brothers cried 'what has G-d done to us', until 'Ani Yosef' revealed that all had been for the good. As salvation nears, the accusing forces fight harder. Sefer Shemos, the book of redemption, repeats this on a larger scale: Moshe appears, the people believe, and the bondage worsens. The Mashgiach applies the pattern to his own era: the hopes after the two world wars and the events in Eretz Yisrael, which the gedolim refused to see as the geulah, since only a redemption from Hashem Himself is eternal. He describes the weakness of today's leadership, like Dasan and Aviram against Moshe, and urges Jews not to despair but to think and speak of Moshiach. He closes with the kitzin that passed in disappointment and teaches that the true ketz is known to no one.

en: At the end of Yosef's twenty-two years of concealment, just when Yaakov sensed hope, the darkness grew worse, until 'Ani Yosef' showed that everything had been for the good.
When the time of salvation approaches, the forces of the sitra achra, which will be nullified by the tikkun, bring accusations, and so the suffering intensifies.
Sefer Shemos repeats on a larger scale the pattern of Yosef's years: when Moshe came and the people believed, the bondage only grew harder.
The gedolim refused a redemption brought about by human hands, since only a geulah from Hashem Himself is eternal.
In the Mashgiach's time, as in Mitzrayim, the people turn away from the quiet Torah leaders toward eloquent, forceful leaders, like Dasan and Aviram against Moshe.
Thinking and speaking about Moshiach binds a Jew to the root of the geulah, since a person is where his thoughts are.
Many kitzin passed in disappointment and were followed by harsh decrees; the true ketz is known to no one, and one must wait for Moshiach every day.

title.en: Yaakov's hope at the end of twenty-two years

summary.en: The Mashgiach calls Sefer Bereishis the foundation of everything and describes Yosef's concealment as an exile. At the end of twenty-two years Yaakov sensed hope in Mitzrayim, yet instead Shimon and Binyamin were taken and his last hopes were dashed.

title.en: 'Ani Yosef' and the accusation before salvation

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the brothers' cry and the revelation 'Ani Yosef', which showed retroactively that all had been good, and brings the Zohar that Hashem will likewise appease Klal Yisrael. He explains that the darkness grows just before salvation because the forces that will be nullified bring accusations.

title.en: Sefer Shemos: exile as a toil of tikkun

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that Sefer Shemos, the book of redemption, repeats the pattern of Yosef's years, and that the bondage in Mitzrayim was a tikkun for the souls of the generations of the flood and the dispersion. He adds that today the same tikkun can be achieved through toil in Torah and avodas Hashem.

title.en: The long nights of Teves and the signs of the times

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the weeks of Shemos to Mishpatim in the long nights of Teves as a time of middas hadin and of tikkun, and points to current events as signs. He tells how the Chofetz Chaim took a flood of the far-off Mississippi River as a sign of judgment, and teaches that the world is a Torah from which one must learn.

title.en: Moshe's coming, and hopes in the Mashgiach's era

summary.en: The Mashgiach shows how after Moshe's coming the bondage worsened, just as with Yaakov and the brothers. He applies this to his era: the tzaddikim felt the end of exile, hopes rose with the world wars and the events in Eretz Yisrael, but the true geulah and the third Beis Hamikdash will come from Hashem alone, not through human hands.

title.en: Refusing a redemption through human hands

summary.en: The Mashgiach brings the Chasam Sofer that there were times when the nations would have returned Eretz Yisrael, and the gedolim refused, since only a redemption from Heaven lasts; Moshe likewise refused the malach. He adds that great redemptions are preceded by korbanos, and that the korbanos of his generation must also be a preparation for something.

title.en: Dasan and Aviram, and waiting for the morning

summary.en: The Mashgiach says that for the third time Klal Yisrael cries 'what has G-d done to us', and compares the leadership of his day to Dasan and Aviram, eloquent and forceful, against Moshe who was no speaker. He brings the Midrash on 'mishomrim laboker': even when the first light disappoints, one must not despair but keep waiting.

title.en: Yaakov looked at our generation

summary.en: The Mashgiach notes that after Yosef and the brothers died the Jews were left without leaders, but Hashem lives. He explains that when Yaakov spoke of the end of days he saw our weak generation and pitied it, and that his advice was to gather and speak of the redemption; he brings the Sforno that Yaakov's last words were a will to keep his way of life.

title.en: Binding oneself to the heichal of Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains that a person is where his thoughts are, so one who thinks of Moshiach is in the heichal of Moshiach, the source of all salvations. He brings the Rambam that awaiting Moshiach is a principle of emunah, and pesukim from Chavakuk, Yeshayahu, Daniel and Eichah on hoping even in the time of hester panim.

title.en: Aleinu, and tzaddikim who waited for Moshiach

summary.en: The Mashgiach explains Aleinu at the end of davening as a binding to Moshiach before going out into the street of exile. He tells of a tzaddik who kept a post by his bed for Moshiach's donkey and leapt from the mikveh thinking Moshiach had come, and of the Chofetz Chaim sitting outside waiting, and teaches that one's joy at the geulah will match one's hope.

title.en: The kitzin of 5408 and 5600

summary.en: The Mashgiach describes the kitzin that passed in disappointment: the Zohar's year 5408 brought the Chmielnicki decrees, exactly the accusation seen with Yosef and Moshe. He explains that the true ketz is hidden, and that the year 5600, when the gates of wisdom were to open, began the scientific revolution, which the nations seized.

title.en: Later kitzin, and the ketz no one knows

summary.en: The Mashgiach lists later dates of hope: the Malbim's calculation followed by the First World War, the year 5701 that brought the Holocaust, and 5728 after the Six Day War, when the land was freed but Yiddishkeit worsened. He concludes that, like Moshe's burial place, the true ketz is known to no one, and one must hope for it every day.

catalogTitle: קיום בנ"י בגלות ע"י בטחון בה' והבדלה מדרכי הגוים

oneLiner.en: The Mashgiach teaches from Parshas Shemos that the Jewish people survives exile through bitachon in Hashem and by keeping apart from the ways of the nations, contrasting Yosef, who was sent to Egypt against his will, with Dasan and Aviram, whose lack of trust led them to seek a place among the Egyptians.

abstract.en: The Mashgiach opens with the Ramban: Sefer Bereishis is a sign of what will happen to the children, and Sefer Shemos is the book of geulah. It is read in the dark weeks of Teves, so learning it lifts a Jew above the darkness. Through the 'futurama' of Bereishis he shows that Yaakov's wish to live in peace was cut off because this world cannot hold the joy of the days of Moshiach. Amram comforted the believers in Egypt, revealing that their suffering repaired the sins of earlier generations. From the Gemara on names he explains that every Jew has a name and a mission, and reads 'asher sam shamos ba'aretz' as missions, not mere wonders. Finally he traces Dasan and Aviram's downfall to leaving over the manna, a lack of bitachon that sent them to study among the Egyptians, unlike Yosef, who was forced and protected.

en: Sefer Shemos is the book of geulah, and learning it in the dark season of Teves connects a Jew to something above the rule of this world.
Even when the great tzaddikim of a generation are gone, the G-d of Israel has not died; He still leads the Jewish people with a hidden hand.
This world is not the stage for the joy of the days of Moshiach; that is why Yaakov's wish to live in peace was cut off.
Every Jew and every generation is sent with a mission, hinted in his name; the hardships that cause wonder are missions whose answers will be revealed in the time of tikun.
Bitachon is the key that has kept Jews alive in exile, both for their livelihood and in their avodas Hashem.
Dasan and Aviram's downfall began with leaving over the manna: lacking bitachon, they sought careers and studied among the Egyptians, unlike Yosef, who was in Egypt against his will.
